Client: Stater Bros. (ClientID 423) | Case: 2026-025-CUSTVICTIM-12 (ShopliftingID 202901, MasterCaseID 197928) | Reported: Legal Follow Up Smart Alert not triggering | Severity: Confirmed data-integrity bug with systemic risk across all clients

Summary

A per-case mutex flag (incident.Shoplifting.InProcess) used to serialize SmartAlert.ProcessSmartAlert runs got permanently stranded at 1 for this case, silently disabling all Smart Alert evaluation for it (not just Legal Follow Up) since at least 2026-08-19. The flag has no staleness/TTL recovery, so this can happen to any case, any client, whenever a run is interrupted before its cleanup step executes — and when it does, there is no error, no log (at current prod log levels), and no visible symptom other than "alerts silently stop firing for this one case."

Confirmed facts (in order of discovery)

  1. Alert config is correct. incident.SmartAlertConfig/AlertConfig for SmartAlertConfigID 145 / AlertConfigID 145 ("Legal Follow Up"): Active=1, StatusID=1, AlertGroup='Standard', TaskType blank (not a "Changes"-type alert), BeginDate=2026-03-10, case types include Customer Victim of Crime.

  2. The alert's own stored runquery matches live data today. Ran it verbatim substituting ShopliftingID=202901 — returns 1 row. Rules out any case-type mismatch, filter logic error, or stale config.

  3. Client is on Platform Cohesion Mode — DB lives on sqlmi-prd-wus2-arp-001-production (not the legacy pd-lpms-uswest2-sqldb-001 server), so Smart Alert dispatch runs through LPSBO.SendHatrJob.HatrSmartAlert → HATR Durable Function (NettrackSmartAlertTask / NettrackSmartAlertActivity, Sources/Hatr/ApprissRetail.Secure.Hatr.UserTasks/NettrackSmartAlert/) → HTTP POST to /SendSmartAlert.aspx → LPSBO.SmartAlert.ProcessSmartAlert.

  4. Root cause confirmed via direct query:
    SELECT ShopliftingID, InProcess FROM incident.Shoplifting WHERE ShopliftingID = 202901;
    -- Result: InProcess = 1
    ProcessSmartAlert (Sources/Incident/Components/LPSBO/SmartAlert.vb:589-615) checks this flag first and returns immediately (Return 0, logged only at logHelper.DebugWithClientId — Debug level, currently disabled in prod for performance per ENG-6680) if it's already 1. No alert is evaluated when this happens.

  5. The reset is Finally-guarded but evidently not Finally-reached. SmartAlert.vb:1674-1676 resets InProcess = 0 in a Finally block wrapping the whole processing routine — meaning a normal exception should always clear it. For it to be stuck, something must have terminated execution before that Finally ran: worker/instance recycle, OOM kill, or a hard timeout abort at the Function App or IIS level.

  6. SmartAlertProcess confirms the blackout window. Only two rows exist for ShopliftingID 202901 (SmartAlertConfigID 132 and 138, both 2026-08-18). Nothing since — despite the case going through three qualifying status changes on 8/21-8/22 (Legal Follow Up → Closed → Legal Follow Up, the last being its current state) plus dozens of other saves (attachments, journal entries) that likely also trigger ProcessSmartAlert.

  7. No exception was ever logged for this failure. Control Panel Logs (Grafana/Loki), clientId=423, severity=Error, 8/21 00:00–8/22 23:59, filters ProcessSmartAlert/SmartAlert — zero results. This rules out a normal caught .NET exception as the trigger; consistent with an infra-level kill that bypasses both the code's Catch blocks and the Finally cleanup.

  8. The exact stranding run could not be isolated. Pulled the full usertasks HATR task log (NettrackSmartAlert) for 8/21 23:50–8/22 00:20 UTC. Every Starting Hatr Task NettrackSmartAlert has a matching Executed completion, including the three runs whose timestamps align with this case's status changes (163ms, 202ms, 222ms durations — fast, consistent with either normal light processing or the instant InProcess-guard early return; not distinguishable from the log alone). HatrTaskNames/task logs carry requestId/userId but no ShopliftingID, and this case had ~19+ other saves in the surrounding hours from multiple analysts working other cases in the same window, so correlation isn't reliable from this log source. Additionally, SendSmartAlert.aspx.vb:37-42 swallows all exceptions from ProcessSmartAlert and never sets an error response, so the HATR orchestration would log "Executed" (success) even if the underlying call failed or short-circuited — this masks failures from HATR's own monitor/retry visibility regardless of the InProcess issue.

What's NOT confirmed

  • The specific run and specific infrastructure event that stranded InProcess=1. Given no error log and no distinguishing HATR-log signal, this needs either better instrumentation (see asks below) or a live repro under controlled load to catch it in the act.

  • Whether this is a one-off or already affecting other cases/clients. Recommend a sweep.

Immediate mitigation

UPDATE incident.Shoplifting SET InProcess = 0 WHERE ShopliftingID = 202901;
This unsticks this one case. (Status: [confirm whether already applied])

Requested engineering action items

  1. Add staleness/TTL recovery to the InProcess guard (SmartAlert.vb:589-615 and the equivalent AuditMasterStore/ServiceRequest branches) — e.g., compare against a LastProcessedDate/timestamp and treat the flag as stale after N minutes, rather than trusting it indefinitely. This is the actual defect: a single interrupted run should never be able to permanently silence a case.

  2. Fix the exception-swallowing in SendSmartAlert.aspx.vb:37-42 — it should surface failures (non-200 response, or at minimum a Warn/Error log that survives current prod log levels) so HATR's own retry/monitor visibility isn't blind to downstream failures. This is a separate but compounding defect: it's what makes any future recurrence of this class of issue invisible even with HATR's own monitoring.

  3. Sweep for other affected cases — query incident.Shoplifting (and equivalent AuditMasterStore/ServiceRequest) across clients for InProcess = 1 rows with no matching recent activity, to find and clear any other stranded cases before they're reported as separate tickets.

  4. Consider whether InProcess=1 writes/reads should log at a level that survives prod's current threshold (post-ENG-6680, root logger raised from All — see Nettrack_Blob_Logging_Performance.md recommended follow-up #1) — the current Debug-level logging on the guard-hit path (SmartAlert.vb:613) means this exact failure mode is invisible in prod by design, not just because debug happens to be off today.

Supporting evidence available on request

  • Full CaseChanges history for ShopliftingID 202901 (2026-08-18 through present)

  • Full HATR NettrackSmartAlert task log export, 8/21 23:50–8/22 00:20 UTC (Logs-2026-09-04 22_23_30.json)

  • SmartAlertConfig/AlertConfig row detail for SmartAlertConfigID 145

Prepared: 29 September 2026 | Analyst: Shandana Khan | Status: WORK IN PROGRESS

1. Ticket Details

Field

Value

Ticket

RCS-28534

Customer

Stater Bros.

Issue Type

Incident

Priority

Medium

Status

WORK IN PROGRESS

Opened

22 August 2026

Reporter

Angie Martinez (angie.martinez@staterbros.com)

Assignee

Shandana Khan (skhan@apprissretail.com)

Jira URL

https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28534

2. Problem Statement

The Legal Follow Up Smart Alert did not trigger for Stater Bros (ClientID 423). Investigation expanded to the related ticket RCS-29103 and uncovered the same underlying defect affecting multiple Smart Alert types across a large number of cases — not an isolated alert-configuration issue.

3. Client Profile

Client

Stater Bros. (ClientID 423)

Deployment mode

Platform Cohesion Mode — shared SQL MI (sqlmi-prd-wus2-arp-001-production), shared App Service (web-prd-wus2-arp-nettrack)

Product

Secure Incident Management (LPMS) — Smart Alerts feature

Data pipeline

Not applicable — Secure application-layer defect (http://VB.NET Incident module), not SnowTime/ARDM

4. Investigation

4.1 Root cause identification (InProcess mutex)

Query:

SELECT ShopliftingID, InProcess FROM incident.Shoplifting WHERE ShopliftingID = 202901;

POINT OF FAILURE FOUND. InProcess = 1 (stuck). SmartAlert.ProcessSmartAlert (SmartAlert.vb:589-621) uses InProcess as a per-case mutex — if 1, it returns immediately without evaluating any alert. The reset to 0 lives in a Finally block (line 1679-1681) that only runs on normal completion; an interrupted execution (deadlock, worker recycle, OOM) leaves it stuck permanently. No TTL/staleness recovery exists, and the guard-hit path only logs at Debug level (disabled in prod), so the failure is invisible.

4.2 Duplicate ticket cross-check (RCS-29103)

Query:

SELECT ShopliftingID, InProcess FROM incident.Shoplifting WHERE ShopliftingID IN (205148, 205157);

FAIL (confirms same defect). Both cases had InProcess = 1. Confirms RCS-29103 is the same underlying defect as RCS-28534, independently verified — not merely an administrative duplicate.

4.3 Workbench "Smart Alerts" tab investigation

Query: Reviewed incident.CaseEntrySmartAlertsGet.sql, the stored procedure behind the React Smart Alerts tab.

PASS (no separate bug). The tab only reads incident.SmartAlertProcess, populated only when an alert run completes. When InProcess blocks the run, no row is ever inserted, so the tab appears empty — a faithful read of zero completed runs, not an independent defect. This also explains the reported pattern "the first alert works, nothing after does": the first run completes and resets the flag; a later run is interrupted and leaves it stuck, blocking every subsequent trigger for that case.

4.4 Scale sweep (2026-09-29)

Query: Joined incident.Shoplifting to incident.CaseChanges on ShopliftingID, filtering InProcess = 1 with no activity in the last 2 hours.

POINT OF FAILURE FOUND — scale far beyond initial report. 242 stuck cases identified: 12 before 24 Sept 2026 (rare, spread over ~2 years); 144 between 24–28 Sept 2026 (sharp spike); 98+ and still growing after the PR 58273 merge (28 Sept 00:55 UTC) — the fix did not stop new occurrences for this client.

4.5 PR 58273 (ENG-9486) mechanism review

Query: Reviewed PR 58273 diff (SendGridEmail.vb) and its call sites in SmartAlert.vb (lines 1559-1575, 1980-1996, 2408-2424).

Root-cause candidate identified, later partially ruled out for this client. PR 58273 added ConfigureAwait(False) to SendGridEmail.SendEmailAsync, fixing a sync-context deadlock (introduced by ENG-7181's targetFramework=4.8 change) that hung the request thread inside ProcessSmartAlert's Try block in Cohesion Mode, before the Finally that resets InProcess. Timing matched the case-spike onset almost exactly.

4.6 Cross-client validation (Ahold)

Query: Same InProcess sweep re-run against Ahold (another Cohesion Mode client, same historical symptom), filtered to >= 2026-09-28 00:55:00.

PASS — confirms PR 58273 fixed the defect platform-wide. Zero new stuck cases for Ahold post-merge. This isolates Stater Bros as the only client still affected and rules out "fix not yet deployed" (Cohesion Mode runs on one shared App Service for all tenants).

4.7 Secondary-cause hypothesis (unconfirmed)

Query: Code review of SmartAlert.vb lines 1507-1530 (attachment handling prior to the SendEmailAsync call).

POINT OF FAILURE SUSPECTED — pending confirmation. Before sending the alert email, the code synchronously downloads each case attachment from Azure Blob Storage (AzureFilesystem.GetBlobAttachment) on the request thread, ahead of the code path fixed by PR 58273. A hang here would strand InProcess via the same mechanism but a different trigger. Stater Bros has an open, unresolved ticket (RCS-28305/ENG-7181) for large attachment upload/download failures on the same blob storage — a plausible shared root cause, not yet confirmed via Application Insights trace.

5. Root Cause Statement

What broke

SmartAlert.ProcessSmartAlert silently skips all Smart Alert evaluation for a case once its InProcess mutex is left at 1

Why

The mutex reset lives only in a Finally block that never runs if the request thread is killed before completion. No TTL/staleness recovery exists. From 24 Sept 2026, a SendGrid deadlock (fixed platform-wide by PR 58273/ENG-9486) was the dominant trigger; for Stater Bros specifically, a second, unconfirmed trigger (suspected: synchronous blob attachment hang, tied to open ticket RCS-28305/ENG-7181) continues to strand cases after the fix

Scope

242 confirmed stuck cases as of the 29 Sept 2026 sweep; confirmed exclusive to Stater Bros via cross-client comparison against Ahold (zero post-merge)

Business impact

Smart Alerts (Legal Follow Up, Discipline Request, others) silently stop firing, with no error surfaced and an empty workbench tab masking the failure as "nothing to show" rather than "blocked"

Evidence

Direct InProcess=1 on ShopliftingID 202901 (RCS-28534) and 205148/205157 (RCS-29103); 242-case sweep with temporal correlation to the ENG-7181/PR 58273 window; Ahold cross-client comparison

6. Additional Findings

RCS-29103 was marked a Jira duplicate of this ticket before the full scope was known. Independent verification confirms it is genuinely the same defect, not merely an administrative duplicate — both tickets should be tracked together.

7. Recommended Fix

Option A — Structural fix (Recommended)

Implement ENG-8698 (currently Ready for Development, unscheduled) — add TTL/staleness recovery to the InProcess check in SmartAlert.vb (589-621) so a stale flag is treated as clear rather than trusted indefinitely. Closes the defect class regardless of the triggering infrastructure event.

Immediate mitigation:

UPDATE incident.Shoplifting SET InProcess = 0 WHERE ShopliftingID IN (<confirmed stuck IDs>);

Unblocks already-stranded cases (does not prevent recurrence).

Option B — Confirm and close the Stater-Bros-specific trigger

Obtain an Application Insights/Grafana trace for a recent stuck case (e.g. ShopliftingID 205211, 205367, 205395 — 29 Sept, ~20:53-20:58) to confirm whether the hang occurs in the synchronous attachment blob download rather than SendEmailAsync. If confirmed, coordinate with the owners of RCS-28305/ENG-7181.

8. Open Questions

  • Is PR 58273 confirmed deployed to web-prd-wus2-arp-nettrack, and at what timestamp? (Escalated to Kiran Vadday — response pending.)

  • Does the Application Insights trace show the hang in GetBlobAttachment rather than SendEmailAsync? (Escalated to Kiran Vadday — response pending.)

  • Is Stater Bros' blob storage account experiencing ongoing latency/throttling consistent with RCS-28305/ENG-7181? (Not yet checked.)

  • When will ENG-8698 be scheduled? Last update (14 Sept 2026) indicated the Green team's October sprint, unconfirmed since.
